commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): restart a dead-but-mapped agent instead of stranding it (#858)
commits.body:
The AgentManager treated presence in the in-memory agents Map as proof an
agent is alive. A dead-but-mapped agent (crash-halted, or a PTY that
exited without the map entry being cleared) could not be restarted:
inspectAgentOp returned DEDUPED and startAgent queued a pendingRestart
and returned without spawning, so status misreported the agent as running
and start/restart silently no-op'd.

Determine real liveness from the AgentProcess status plus an OS-level pid
probe (process.kill(pid, 0)) rather than map membership:

- inspectAgentOp only DEDUPs a start against a genuinely-alive entry.
- startAgent evicts a dead entry and starts fresh instead of queueing a
  pendingRestart. A synchronous evictingAgents guard, claimed before the
  eviction await and released in finally, prevents concurrent same-name
  starts from double-spawning a PTY during the await window.
- getAllStatuses reports a running entry whose pid is gone as stopped.

The 'starting' state is treated as alive with no pid check so the existing
BUG-011 in-flight-restart dedup is preserved; the alive path (including
the daemonJustCrashed branch) is unchanged.

Adds tests/unit/daemon/agent-manager-liveness.test.ts covering eviction,
dedup preservation, status correction, and the concurrent-eviction guard.

Inspired by community reports #757 (staleness detector) and #620
(pid-alive spawn verification).

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): stop a disabled agent from being resurrected by crash recovery (#859)
commits.body:
* fix(daemon): stop a disabled agent from being resurrected by crash recovery

A deliberately stopped or disabled agent could come back on its own via two
paths:

1. AgentProcess.handleExit() respawns the agent (image-poison and
   exponential-backoff crash recovery) gated only on stopRequested/stopping
   and isDaemonShuttingDown() — never on whether the agent has been disabled.
   A disabled agent that force-exits or crashes with stopRequested=false was
   respawned, resurrecting a stood-down agent.
2. AgentManager.stopAgent() honors a queued pendingRestarts entry. A restart
   queued during a user stop/disable (the BUG-011 restart-all race window)
   would fire after the stop and bring the agent back up.

Fix:

- handleExit now returns early when a .user-disable marker is present
  (isUserDisabled(), mirroring the existing .daemon-stop/isDaemonShuttingDown
  pattern), before crash counting and before both respawn timers, and marks
  the agent stopped. The marker is written by `cortextos disable` and cleared
  in start() so a re-enabled agent recovers from crashes again.
- stopAgent(name, userInitiated=false): an explicit user stop/disable
  (the stop-agent IPC handler passes true) drops any queued pendingRestart so
  the stop wins. restartAgent and stopAll keep the default false, so the
  restart-all honor path (BUG-011/BUG-031) is unchanged.

Adds unit tests: a disabled agent's force-exit does not crash-recover; start()
clears the marker so a re-enabled agent recovers again; a user-initiated stop
drops a queued restart while an internal restart-all still honors it.

Inspired by community reports #807 (isEnabled gate on exit) and #619
(restart-marker hygiene).

* fix(daemon): restore cortextos restart under the stop-wins change

Round-1 made the stop-agent IPC handler pass userInitiated=true for every
stop, so an explicit stop/disable drops a queued pendingRestart. But
cortextos restart is a client-side stop-agent + start-agent sequence, and the
stop-agent handler is fire-and-forget: the follow-up start races in while the
agent is still registered, is deduped into a pendingRestart, and the
unconditional userInitiated=true then dropped it, leaving the agent stopped.

Thread userInitiated through the IPCRequest: the handler now uses
request.userInitiated ?? true (so cortextos stop / stop --all / disable keep
the stay-down behavior), and cortextos restart's stop-half sends
userInitiated=false so its own raced-in start is honored via the pendingRestart
path. restart writes .user-stop (not .user-disable), so the disable
resurrection gate never blocks it.

Adds tests/unit/cli/restart-command.test.ts asserting restart sends
userInitiated=false plus a follow-up start-agent (fails against the regressed
code), and an agent-manager honor test locking the contract the fix depends on.

---------

Co-authored-by: Boris <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(pty): surface a wedged first-run prompt and validate working_directory (#860)
commits.body:
The daemon auto-accepts Claude Code's first-run trust/bypass screens, but if
the PTY parks on a prompt the matcher misses (or one rendering after the
backstop), the agent sits wedged while status still reports it "running" — the
wedge is invisible. An invalid working_directory also spawned silently or
failed cryptically.

Observability + robustness (the auto-accept keystroke logic from a15baad4 is
unchanged):

- At the auto-accept backstop, if the PTY is still parked on a first-run prompt
  and never bootstrapped, set an "awaiting interactive confirmation" flag and
  log a warning. AgentProcess.getStatus() surfaces it as a new optional
  AgentStatus.awaitingConfirmation, and `cortextos status` renders it as
  "unhealthy*" with a footnote. The getter is AND-gated with !isBootstrapped()
  so a late recovery auto-reports healthy.
- Validate working_directory at spawn: throw a clear error on a whitespace-only
  or nonexistent path. The empty string is the framework's "unset" sentinel
  (import-agent writes working_directory: '') and still falls through to
  agentDir, so imported agents are unaffected. Covers AgentPTY-derived runtimes
  (claude/hermes/opencode); codex-app-server has no first-run TUI.
- Broaden the auto-accept token match (Bypass/bypass + accept; trust +
  folder/directory) via a shared detector, still co-occurring tokens only, and
  extend the backstop 20s -> 45s for slow first-runs.
- Harden the invariant structurally: the poll stops the instant the session
  bootstraps, before evaluating any prompt branch, so no stray keystroke can
  ever reach a live session.

Adds unit tests for working_directory validation, wedge detection, the
broadened tokens, the status surfacing, and the no-keystroke-into-live-session
invariant.

Inspired by community report #623 (restart-into-wedge detection).

commits.body:
The status table showed a bare "-" for agents with no explicit model
override, identical to the pid/uptime absent-markers and reading as
missing/error. An unset model means the agent runs the inherited system
default, so render "default" to make that state legible. Matches the
existing "defaults to org default" wording used for the --model option.

Adds a focused unit test asserting the default label and verbatim
rendering of an explicit model.

+# Lifecycle status schemas
+
+These checked-in JSON Schemas are the normative machine-readable contracts for
+`cortextos lifecycle status`.
+
+`cortext.status/v1` and `cortext.status.redacted/v1` describe the legacy bridge
+profile only. Managed lifecycle profiles will use a future discriminated
+contract instead of placing non-null managed evidence into this legacy shape.
+Check results bind each policy to its exact v1 identifier and require empty
+reasons on pass or at least one unique policy-specific reason on failure.
+Passing results are additionally bound to the snapshot facts required by the
+policy evaluator; the legacy `update-safe` policy has no passing schema branch.
+Healthy summaries and checks require a running, responsive daemon and canonical
+info-only observations; usable checks reject canonical blocking observations.
+Observations that make legacy collection incomplete are declared once in the
+shared partial-observation manifest; collectors, redaction, checks, schemas, and
+data-driven mutation tests all consume that invariant.
+Observation codes are bound to their fixed severity and domain. Redacted error
+codes are likewise bound to one static message and detail code. Redacted
+capabilities, observations, isolation evidence, and version strings are closed
+public surfaces, and report identifiers and observation days use their exact
+emitted formats. The redactor reconstructs observation metadata and derived
+overall fields before recomputing checks rather than copying untrusted
+assertions or strings.
+
+When a status type changes, update its schema and the corresponding TypeScript
+type together. Run the focused lifecycle and schema tests before committing:
+
+```bash
+npm test -- --run tests/unit/lifecycle/legacy-status.test.ts tests/unit/lifecycle/status-schema.test.ts
+npm run build && node scripts/verify-lifecycle-status-cli.mjs
+```
+
+The schema tests validate emitted local and redacted snapshots, both error
+envelopes, and recursive rejection of additional redacted properties. Schema
+generation is intentionally not part of dependency installation: contributors
+on every supported Node version receive the same reviewed contracts without an
+additional code-generation supply chain.

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): validate CronEntry shape and clarify config.json docs (#886)
commits.body:
* fix(daemon): validate CronEntry shape and clarify config.json docs

CronEntry (config.json) has no `enabled` field, but the crons.json
(CronDefinition) example block sat directly above it showing
enabled: true, priming the mistake of adding it to a config.json
entry — where convertEntry() silently drops it and the cron migrates
live regardless of intent.

Add validateCronEntryShape() to flag any CronEntry key/type outside
the closed schema before conversion (advisory, non-blocking), annotate
the doc-comment block to make the CronDefinition-only scope explicit,
and mark the type:"once" future-fire_at skip as UNMIGRATABLE since
CronDefinition has no fire_at support yet and that skip is a real gap,
not a routine one.

Scoped to the framework-level fix only; fleet-wide per-agent
remediation of already-migrated entries is tracked separately
(task_1786109257679_17674175, owned by paul).

* fix(daemon): bind CronEntry key validation to the type at compile time

KNOWN_CRON_ENTRY_KEYS was a hand-maintained Set literal with no link back
to the CronEntry interface, so a field added to/removed from CronEntry
would silently desync from the validator with no compiler signal. Derive
it from a Record<keyof CronEntry, true> object instead, so any drift
between the two is a TS error (excess or missing property) at build time.

Per paul, gate requirement (A) on task_1786109049618_21237062 / PR #886.

* fix(daemon): gate unrecognised cron-entry keys/types per-entry, not per-agent

validateCronEntryShape's warnings previously only logged; migration proceeded
unconditionally even for malformed entries (e.g. the live data-agent
type:"crontab" shape). Any warning now refuses that single entry outright
before convertEntry is attempted (cronsRefused on MigrationResult), while
every other entry for the same agent still migrates - a whole-agent abort
would reproduce the exact silent-loss failure shape this is meant to fix.

migrate-crons CLI exits non-zero when any entry was refused, so the gate is
checkable by exit code rather than by reading log text.

Also reworded the past-fire_at skip: convertEntry has no fire-history lookup
anywhere in its call chain, so "already fired or expired" overstated what is
verifiable. Reworded to state only what is known.

---------

commits.author: Aaron Sachs
commits.subject: perf(dashboard): read each agent's execution log once in GET /crons (#875)
commits.body:
readLastExecution(agent, cronName) re-read and re-parsed the agent's
entire cron-execution.log once PER CRON. At 10 crons per agent that is
ten full reads of the same file per request. /health already read each
agent's log exactly once, which is why it benchmarked several times
faster than /crons over the same dataset.

One backward pass per agent now builds a Map<cronName, lastEntry>;
keeping the first hit per name preserves "last entry in file order wins"
exactly. Cost is O(agents) reads instead of O(crons).

Measured on tests/integration/phase4-performance.test.ts:
  50 crons:  p50 79.0ms -> 19.4ms,  p95 88.7ms -> 21.5ms
  100 crons: p50 76.3ms -> 18.0ms,  p95 77.3ms -> 18.8ms

commits.subject: fix(cli): list-tasks renders full ids + supports --project filter (#816)
commits.body:
Three related defects around the list-tasks surface:

1. Text table truncated every 27-char task id to 26 chars AND padded the
   id column to exactly its own width, gluing the assignee straight onto
   the id. Copying an id out of the table produced a plausible-but-wrong
   value. The table now sizes the id/assignee columns from the data (same
   pattern as the crons table), never truncates ids, keeps 2+ spaces
   between all columns, and marks title truncation with an ellipsis.
   Rendering is extracted to an exported formatTaskTable() with
   regression tests.

2. Orchestrator templates instruct 'list-tasks --project human-tasks'
   but the option did not exist; with stderr suppressed the failing
   command read as '0 stale human tasks' (silent false negative).
   listTasks() and the CLI now support --project, and the template drops
   the error-suppressing 2>/dev/null on the detector path.

3. .gitignore's 'node_modules/' matches only real directories, so a
   symlinked node_modules (worktree checkouts) evaded it — the mechanism
   of a past committed-symlink incident. Now 'node_modules' without the
   slash.
